propositions: A failed identity write (add_label or set_entity_property) after successful issue creation calls delete_issue on the created Jira issue, destroying recoverable work and stranding the local ticket in a keyed-pending binding that retro-attach cannot fix.

The rollback delete is redundant because record_pending_key records the key durably before identity writes, and recover_pending's keyed branch already exists to retro-attach labels and properties deterministically without search in exactly this window state.

The Jira error 'Field cannot be set. It is not on the appropriate screen' is misleading, occurring in three distinct scenarios: field absent from Create/Edit screen, jira.permission.createclone.denied workflow property set, or malformed field value on a screen-present field.

After the rollback delete, the keyed-pending binding is never unbound, so subsequent recover_pending passes repeatedly attempt add_label on the deleted key, fail, and leave the entry permanently stuck pending.

The current behavior choice between a clean rollback-delete and a permanently-stuck retro-attach binding is a design decision trading off deleted work versus stuck repair; both cases require explicit argument given _call_with_retry has already filtered transient failures.
